target_customer: Retailers and distributors running warehouses and distribution centers that manually pick and palletize cases
problem: Case picking and mixed-SKU palletizing remain largely manual, costing US retailers over $10B a year in labor by the company's estimate, while existing automation costs $100M to $350M per warehouse or $300k to $500k per large robot.
business_model: Robotics as a service or hardware installation into existing warehouses (reported by an aggregator, pricing not disclosed)
product_category: Warehouse robotics, swarm case picking and palletizing

founders.name: Eric Miller
founders.background_notes: Five years at Skydio, founded and grew its Autonomy Infrastructure team per the YC launch post.

founders.name: Nathan Yee
founders.background_notes: Four years of machine learning and robot software experience, multi-robot scheduling. One database lists him as CEO, so titles conflict.

competitors.name: Boston Dynamics Stretch
competitors.what: Mobile manipulator for truck unloading with mixed-case palletizing on its roadmap
competitors.traction_then: DHL announced a $15M investment in Boston Dynamics robots in January 2022 starting with Stretch
competitors.funding_then: Boston Dynamics is a large well funded company

competitors.name: Pickle Robot
competitors.traction_then: In production at several sites by late 2022
competitors.funding_then: $26M Series A in November 2022, about $32M total

technical_complexity.rationale: Swarm robots driving upside down on an overhead steel plate with vacuum grippers, wireless mesh coordination, collision avoidance and orchestration software require hardware and multi-robot planning that a six person team had to build from scratch.

defensibility.rationale: Novel mechanical architecture and orchestration may be patentable and hard to copy quickly, but there are no disclosed customers or patents in sources, and hardware robotics is capital intensive.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded players targeted palletizing and truck unloading with arms and mobile manipulators. No sourced move against AutoPallet found as of early 2026.

market_need_then: The company cites over 30 billion cases moved manually each year and over $10B in labor. Customers faced high cost and slow install of conveyor and arm based systems.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain engineering tone with ROI targets (under 12 months) in its YC launch post.

branding.brand_signature: Robots that drive upside down on an overhead plate, shown at Manifest 2026
branding.community_and_virality: February 2026 trade coverage of its first public demo at Manifest.

brand_strength.rationale: Very early company with trade press only around a demo. No sourced brand assets beyond the product concept.

outcome_analysis: AutoPallet is an early hardware startup still active. Its sourced milestones are the YC S24 batch, a launch post with design targets but no customers, and a first public demo at Manifest in February 2026. With no verified funding or customers, no success or failure story can be told yet.
notes: Unverified funding: aggregators (Caplight, Standout, Preqin, Crunchbase) report a seed of about $500K from Pioneer Fund and Y Combinator in September 2024, Dealroom shows $125K. Not recorded as a round. YC launch post names no competitors, so the list comes from trade sources and a Boston Dynamics brochure. Dexterity was searched but nothing sourced found.
